title: RR, Hr, MDR, pre-XDR, XDR
dek: Definitions moved in 2021. MDR is still INH+RIF. Pre-XDR adds a FQ. XDR adds BDQ or LZD on top of MDR/RR+FQ. A 2015 “XDR” paper is a different object.
story: Rifampin-resistant TB (RR-TB) is operationally the Xpert-era door to second-line algorithms. Many RR isolates are also INH-R (MDR-TB: resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampin). Some are INH-S — still not HRZE. Hr-TB is INH-R, RIF-S — a different recipe (6REZ-Lfx).

WHO 2021: pre-XDR-TB = MDR/RR plus fluoroquinolone resistance. XDR-TB = MDR/RR plus FQ plus at least one Group A drug (bedaquiline or linezolid). The old XDR (MDR + FQ + a second-line injectable) was retired because injectables left the preferred regimens.

Surveillance, papers, and lab reports still mix eras. If a 2018 dataset says XDR, ask which definition. If a genome is FQ-R but BDQ/LZD naive, it is pre-XDR, not 2021-XDR, even if it would have been “XDR” in 2015 via amikacin.
deepTitle: Why the injectable retirement matters in a BAM
deep: rrs 1401 a>g still exists in genomes and still matters if someone reaches for AMK. It does not make 2021-XDR by itself.

RR on Xpert without INH genotyping is RR, not proven MDR. Treat as RR; do not write MDR in the case notification until INH is known — or follow NTP rules that treat RR as MDR operationally and say so.
Group A is currently BDQ, LZD, FQ. Group letters also moved. Read the year of the guideline you are citing.
Heteroresistance can make a person “MDR” in the cavity and “DS” in the MGIT. Definitions assume a sample.

visual.caption: 2021 WHO nested definitions. Injectables are off the XDR ladder. FQ is the pre-XDR step; BDQ or LZD is the XDR step.

steps.title: 2021 definition is pre-XDR
steps.body: FQ-R yes; BDQ and LZD loci clean. Do not import the archive word into a BPaL eligibility discussion without translating.

steps.title: AMK still dead
steps.body: rrs 1401 remains relevant if someone tries an injectable salvage. It just is not the XDR criterion anymore.

example.takeaway: Translate definitions before you translate regimens.
